## Controlling the killing edge of Geng-metal by joining with it


One way to control the killing energy (살기 殺氣) of Geng-metal (경금 庚金) is simply to join with it (합 合).

From the Body-Qimen view, a flow in which Xun (巽 ☴) meets Qian (乾 ☰) (Heaven-Wind, Gou ䷫ · Dragon Escape), and Kan (坎 ☵ · the Rest Gate 휴문) is then added, interlocks precisely with two principles. The first is the yin-yang union of yin-wood and metal-qi (陰木 + 金氣), as in the Yi-Geng combination (을경합 乙庚合) and the Chen-You combination (진유합 辰酉合). The second is the generating cycle "metal generates water, water generates wood."

Qian ☰ symbolizes strong yang-metal (the very body of Geng 庚). Xun ☴ symbolizes soft yin-wood (Yi-wood 乙). Normally metal and wood collide ("metal overcomes wood"). But when yang-metal (Qian ☰ / Geng) meets yin-wood (Xun ☴ / Yi), they do not fight. They embrace like husband and wife: the yin-yang harmony of the Yi-Geng combination.

So you form the Xun seal with the left hand and the Qian seal with the right. In the Book of Changes, the hexagram where Qian ☰ meets Xun ☴, *Gou* (天風姤 ䷫), means "meeting by chance, yin and yang uniting" (음양상구 陰陽相遘)…

## The White Tiger energy of the Ding-Chou day as fuel


The White Tiger Great Killing (백호대살 白虎大殺) energy of a Ding-Chou day (정축일 丁丑日) works like this. Ding-fire (丁火) is shut inside the "Tomb" stage (묘 墓, tomb or storehouse) of the twelve life stages. It is pressed together with the hidden stems inside Chou-earth (丑土): Gui-water (癸水), Xin-metal (辛金), and Ji-earth (己土). All of this is compressed to an extreme, like high-pressure underground magma ready to burst out at any moment.

Left uncontrolled, this fierce energy shows up as rising blood pressure, sudden mood swings, or stagnant qi in the abdomen (복부 기체 氣滯). But use it as fuel for internal alchemy (내단 內丹), with the sealing force of abdominal pressure (복압 腹壓) and the pressure of breath retention (지식 止息), and it becomes an ultra-high-pressure booster. In one push it drives up the storing of qi (축기 蓄氣) and the piercing of the central channel (중맥 中脈), which would normally take months.

## Why Ding-Chou can be auspicious or ominous, and the hand-seal sequence


Today, a Ding-Chou day, is one of the seven great White Tiger days (백호살) among the sixty cycle days. Its energy is condensed to the extreme. Maybe that's why the market is in such chaos.

In Body-Qimen, the Jade Maiden (옥녀 玉女) carries the energy of Ding-fire. She gently melts the Geng-metal energy that attacks Jia-wood (갑목 甲木).

So depending on the earthly branch it meets, Ding-fire can create an auspicious formation (길격 吉格), or an ominous one (흉격 凶格) in which nothing works.

The mechanism in one sentence: "When Ding-fire (丁火), the moving starlight, enters a particular direction (branch) of the nine palaces, it meets the heavenly stem already lying at the bottom of that direction, the hidden stem (지장간 地藏干), and automatically sparks an auspicious formation (a chemical spark)."

Everything depends on the bond Ding forms with the palace's owner (its stem) at the moment it settles into that palace (branch).

In Body-Qimen this is done with hand seals (수인 手印):

- **Left hand holds Former-Heaven Li ☲** = switch on the heavenly Ding-fire (丁火 · Jade Maiden).
- **Right hand holds one of the six Later-Heaven palaces** (Zhen, Xun, Kun, Dui, Qian, Gen) = call up the hidden stem concealed in that palace's branch (Mao, Si, Wei, You, Hai, Chou).
- **The two hands interlock** = Ding plus the hidden stem combine, and Qimen Dunjia's six great auspicious formations activate inside your own body.

**Why is it sometimes auspicious and sometimes ominous?**

Looking only at the stems, Ding + Xin (丁+辛), Ding + Gui (丁+癸), or Ding-fire entering the Gen palace (Chou-earth), which is called "striking punishment" (격형 擊刑), are classed in space-time Qimen Dunjia as difficult or ominous.

Ding-Chou is the image of Ding-fire, the starlight and candle flame of heaven, set on top of Chou-earth, the frozen winter mud of the ground and the storehouse of metal.

You *can* use the Ding-Chou Jade Maiden as a great auspicious formation: "lighting a lamp to open a dark treasure vault." But if your body's condition (its fire timing, 화후 火候) or the order in which you use the energies is off, Ding-Chou turns into one of the hardest ominous formations in Qimen, destiny reading (명리), and neidan alike.

**1) Fire generates earth, but not every earth welcomes fire.**

- *The nature of Chou-earth:* the Chou month, which holds Minor Cold and Great Cold, is the coldest, darkest stretch of deep winter: frozen, waterlogged mud (습토 濕土).
- *The flame suffocates (회화 晦火):* if the basic yang-qi of the lower belly (lower dantian; Qian-metal ☰) has not been warmed up at all, and you rashly take only the Ding-Chou seal (left Li ☲ + right Gen ☶), the little candle (Ding-fire) is crushed by the damp of the cold mud. It loses its light, smokes, and goes out.
- *Ding-fire enters the tomb (입묘 入墓):* by the twelve life stages, Chou is Ding-fire's tomb (묘지 墓地), where its energy goes into the grave. Go in unprepared and instead of opening the vault, the starlight of your own awareness (the Jade Maiden) gets trapped in a cold tomb. You fall into lethargy, low mood, or deep exhaustion (a drained battery).

**2) Open the belly of the character Chou (its hidden stems)** and three things lie coiled there: Gui-water (癸水, cold rain), Xin-metal (辛金, a sharp gem or needle), and Ji-earth (己土, cloud or damp soil).

If Ding enters Chou with no protective shield, two Qimen ominous formations go off inside the hidden stems at once:

1. **Inner "Red Bird plunges into the river" (주작투강 朱雀投江, Ding + Gui):** the cold Gui-water hidden in Chou-earth rises and smothers Ding-fire's spark (water overcomes fire). In neidan practice this is when cold water (한수 寒水) in the lower belly puts out the faint warmth at the solar plexus. The belly goes cold, with diarrhea or indigestion.
2. **Inner "fire and metal at war" (화금상전 火金相戰, Ding + Xin):** if Ding touches the Xin-metal inside Chou-earth with weak, clumsy fire, it does not refine the gem. It only coats it in soot, and they clash in sparks (fire overcoming metal, backfiring). Qimen reads this as an ominous formation of getting tangled in disputes with a criminal (Xin-metal).

Ding-Chou is one of the seven great White Tiger days, its energy condensed to the extreme. When this high-pressure energy is well gathered in through neidan, it becomes explosive drive and the power to open the treasury (재물 개고 開庫). When control is lost, it shows up as side effects of qi and blood flowing backward in the body: rising blood pressure, sudden anger, muscle cramps, or nerve pain.

In the end, Ding-Chou turns ominous for one reason only: "you shoved a bare little candle (Ding-fire) into a cold, murky storehouse (Chou-earth)."

That is exactly why, when I gave today's Ding-Chou seal sequence earlier, I stressed that you must not go straight to *Bi* (山火賁 ䷕: Ding-Chou). You must first lay down *Great Taming* (山天大畜 ䷙) and then draw it out afterward with *Xian* (澤山咸 ䷞)!

- **Pre-warming (prevents damp earth smothering fire and the Red Bird plunging):** *Great Taming* ䷙, right hand Gen ☶ / left hand Qian ☰. Close all the fingers of the left hand and first shoot the pure yang of the sun (Qian ☰) into palace 8, Gen. The frozen mud and cold water (Gui) of Chou-earth dry out warmly, making a warm hearth where the Jade Maiden's fire will never go out.
- **Feeding in the Jade Maiden (refining the vault):** *Bi* ䷕, right hand Gen ☶ / left hand Li ☲. With the lower belly warm, lift only the left middle finger to switch on Ding-fire (Li ☲). The ominous formations (striking punishment, entering the tomb) vanish. Only the vault inside Chou-earth opens, safely, and the great auspicious formation "Jade Maiden in hidden treasure · opening the Chou-Wei storehouse" (옥녀암장 · 축미개고) starts working.

Put only fire (Li ☲) into palace 8 (Gen) with an empty lower belly and you get "striking punishment," and the energy breaks. But first seal palace 8 shut and fill it with energy, using *Great Taming* ䷙ or *Decrease* (山澤損 ䷨) as we learned before, then switch to *Bi* ䷕. It transforms completely into an auspicious formation: melting the mountain's vault (Chou-earth, the storehouse of metal) with Ding's fire and digging out the gold.
Just leave the ring finger extended. And when you form a mudra (수인 手印), it is better to keep the fingers spread apart so their energies don't overlap.

Following gladly, not dragging by force: Sui ䷐

Following gladly, not dragging by force.
*Lake-Thunder, Following* (택뢰수 澤雷隨 ䷐: outer trigram Dui ☱ + inner trigram Zhen ☳)

*Following* (䷐) is the state in which, once the true qi within (Zhen ☳) first moves on the inside, my awareness and breath (Dui ☱) simply follow behind it softly and gladly (수 隨).

It is the hexagram that most exactly expresses "the mind follows the qi" (심수기 心隨氣: the mind quietly follows the flow of qi) and "neither forget nor help" (물망물조 勿忘勿助: do not forget it, and do not force it along).

"Metal and wood uniting and fire hidden in water," beyond metal overcoming wood (금극목 金剋木), that is, metal and wood joining (금목상합 金木相合) and fire stored in water (수중장화 水中藏火):

The outer trigram Dui (☱) is metal (金, the youngest daughter), and the inner trigram Zhen (☳) is wood (木, the eldest son).

In internal alchemy (내단학 內丹學), joining the Azure Dragon of the east (wood 木 · nature 性 · Zhen ☳) with the White Tiger of the west (metal 金 · feeling 情 · Dui ☱) into one is called "metal and wood merging" (금목교병 金木交倂) or "the dragon and tiger mating" (용호상교 龍虎相交).

The sharp metal (Dui ☱) becomes a soft pond of water and embraces the thunder-wood (Zhen ☳) below. So the yang qi does not explode upward and scatter. Instead its warm vibration of life melts wholly into the cool pond (elixir saliva, jade fluid 단침·옥액), and the finest kind of storing and warm nurturing (온양 溫養) takes place.

"Achievement through going with the grain (순리 順理), and the blessing of people (인복 人福)": even if I don't strain to beat the world by force, by reading the flow of the times and the hearts of others and following flexibly (수 隨), I instead draw people and the world to follow me gladly (천하수지 天下隨之). It brings a powerful affinity and a fortune with a fair wind behind it.

The two-hand seals (수결 手訣) and the asymmetric harmony of the fingertip terminals:

Left hand (Zhen ☳): press only the ring finger (output · Triple Burner) flat against the thumb, one to one, and extend the index and middle fingers.

Tea, the gut, and the Industrial Revolution

The principle of qi that operates in an individual body operates the same way in the history of civilization.

Medieval Europeans drank alcohol (fermented drinks) all day instead of contaminated water, and the whole society was sunk in alcohol-made "damp-phlegm" (습담, turbid qi) and brain fog.

But in the 17th century, as "tea," steeped in boiled water, spread, a huge shift occurred.

According to research by historians such as Alan Macfarlane, the biggest secret behind the population explosion in early Industrial Revolution Britain, even as workers crowded into unsanitary, packed cities, was that the habit of drinking black tea sharply cut deaths from intestinal disease.

With healthy intestines (장 腸), labor productivity and vitality leapt.

The sterilizing power of boiled water and tea washed out gut toxins and waterborne disease, and tea's clear, alert energy cleared away the heavy meat diet and intoxication of Europeans. Once the turbid qi in the belly went down and the collective head cleared, the Enlightenment and the Industrial Revolution finally began.

What we drink, and how we tune the qi of the body, changes a far larger reality than we think.

Emptying the turbid qi downward is what finally lets the upper body (the head) become clear. The physiology of the body and the principle of qi turn together, meshed like this.

Small Taming ䷈: dense clouds, no rain

Bright light simply scatters and disappears if left alone. What matters is gathering that light. That is, what matters is Vairocana Buddha (비로자나불) becoming Vajrasattva (금강살타).

Wind-Heaven, Small Taming (풍천소축 風天小畜 ䷈) is the 9th of the 64 hexagrams. Taken literally it means "wind (風 ☴) blows above heaven (天 ☰), gathering and nurturing (畜) on a small scale (小)."

The most famous line explaining Small Taming in the main text of the *Book of Changes* (the judgment) is "密雲不雨 自我西郊": "dense clouds gather from the western fields until their density peaks, yet they do not yet pour down as rain."

If the clouds (qi) gather and pour out as rain (liquid, semen), the energy discharges and it's over.

It means that, rather than spending or earning showily on the outside, when you consolidate the inner substance (the Gate of Life 명문, the core) and store energy, the great explosive power that follows (Fire-Heaven, Great Possession ䷍) is prepared.

Conclusion (where yin and yang meet and burst): with the lower belly (the two yang lines 1–2 ⚊⚊) supporting and the upper chest (the two yin lines 5–6 ⚋⚋) clear and empty, line 3 (yin ⚋) and line 4 (yang ⚊) touch exactly at the center of the chest and spark yin-yang union. So the structure is one in which the chest chakra cannot help opening wide in every direction without any tightness!

If you draw the "nuclear trigrams" (호괘 互卦: the inner hidden trigrams), the Yijing secret of looking into a hexagram's flesh (the central lines 2–5), you get a spine-tingling explanation of why the heart chakra and eyes brightened.

Za Rahula, the secret of the black sun

[Za Rahula, the secret of the black sun]

Freshly made new-season tea is biased to one side, strong in green wood qi (목기 木氣) or sharp fire qi (화기 火氣). But old tea that has ripened well through thirty years of wind and frost has a tea nature (차성 茶性) that is neither cold nor hot: the perfect "central harmony (중화 中和), the energy of the spring and autumn equinoxes."

The equinoxes are also connected with solar and lunar eclipses.

In Tibetan tantra (especially vase breathing 보병기, tummo, and the secret teachings of Za Rahula), the core aim of practice is to stop the rough winds (karmic winds 업풍 業風) that flow divided in the left channel (moon, yin) and right channel (sun, yang), and push them into the central channel (avadhuti) in the very middle.

The moment the right-hand Dui trigram (☱), symbolizing Zuofu and Youbi (좌보우필, the sun and moon), meets the left-hand Zhen trigram (☳), symbolizing Za Rahula, and the left and right channels overlap at the center of the central channel (an inner solar and lunar eclipse), dualistic tension and afflictions vanish in an instant, and an inexpressible bliss bursts out: "great bliss" (대락 大樂, vast rapture) and "emptiness" (공성 空性, a stillness empty yet full) at once.

This sensation, meshed with the stillness after rain stops, is the experience of "bliss and emptiness are not two" (락공불이 樂空不二). This is the energy of Rahula, and the energy of the Celestial Worthy of the Nine Heavens, Responding to the Origin, Thunder-Sound, Universal Transformation (구천응원뇌성보화천존 九天應元雷聲普化天尊).

Gathering into the central channel like this is called *Lake-Thunder, Following* (택뢰수 澤雷隨 ䷐) in the Yijing.

The Later-Heaven position of thunder (Zhen) is originally, in Former Heaven, where the "sun (Li-fire ☲)" rises (the sun rising from Fusang 일출부상).

The Later-Heaven position of the lake (Dui) is originally, in Former Heaven, where the "moon (Kan-water ☵)" waxes (the moon rising over the western hills 월출서산).

Beneath the Later-Heaven Zhen palace (3) hides the Former-Heaven "sun (Li ☲)," and beneath the Later-Heaven Dui palace (7) hides the Former-Heaven "moon (Kan ☵)"!

So the moment you form the Zhen trigram (☳) with the left hand and the Dui trigram (☱) with the right to make *Following* (䷐), outwardly thunder and lake (Zhen and Dui = spring and autumn equinox) unite. But in the inner Former-Heaven body, the "sun (Li ☲)" of due east and the "moon (Kan ☵)" of due west are drawn into the very center (palace 5, the central palace, the central channel) and overlap face to face: "sun and moon joined like a jade disc" (일월합벽 日月合璧), a total solar and lunar eclipse!

In all the internal-alchemy classics, including the *Zhouyi cantong qi* (주역참동계), the *Wuzhen pian* (오진편), and the *Yonghobigyeol* (용호비결), when circulating the abdominal orbit, passing the eastern Mao position (palace 3 Zhen, spring equinox) and the western You position (palace 7 Dui, autumn equinox) is called "bathing" (목욕 沐浴) and treated as most important.

The hot yang qi rising after the fire is kindled at the winter solstice (palace 1 Kan) (advancing the fire 진화 進火) reaches its mildest climate at the eastern Zhen palace (3, Mao, spring equinox), and after passing the summer solstice (palace 9 Li) and reaching the western Dui palace (7, You, autumn equinox), it becomes clear and cool like an autumn sky.
The classics teach: "At the positions of the spring equinox (Zhen) and autumn equinox (Dui), don't force the breath (the bellows) tight or push it. Empty the mind and let the qi wrap around and wash itself (bathing and warm nurturing 목욕온양)."

In terms of seasons, the perfect mildness of the spring and autumn equinoxes, neither cold nor hot;

astronomically, Za Rahula's solar and lunar eclipse, sun (Former-Heaven Li) and moon (Former-Heaven Kan) becoming one at the node (opening of the central channel);

in five-phase terms, the Chen-You combination into metal (진유합금, the condensation of Vajrasattva), in which eastern wood (Zhen, liver-gallbladder) and western metal (Dui, lungs-large intestine) lock together at the navel center (central palace 5).

Since all happen at once, the nervous system responds immediately and blossoms into rapture (great bliss 대락 大樂), the entrance to deep samadhi.

Vasudhara, the earth womb, and Return ䷗

In the mandalas and mythic lineage of tantra, the eternal consort (명비 明妃 / dakini) of Jambhala (the male wealth deity), the earth goddess who supplies him with the source of abundance, is "Vasudhara" (바수다라).

For Jambhala's blessing (가피) to activate, Vasudhara's activity must begin first.

The meaning of Vasudhara:

Vasu: treasure, gold, goods, the seed of vitality
Dhara: to hold, to sustain, the earth (womb), a flowing river

So Vasudhara literally means "the womb of the earth holding the seed of treasure" (the earth-mother goddess 지모신 地母神); Chinese sutras translate her as "Bodhisattva Who Upholds the World" (지세보살 持世菩薩) or "Heavenly Maiden of the Source of Wealth" (재원천녀 財源天女). It calls to mind Demeter.

If Jambhala is the father (skillful means) who distributes treasure to the world, the mother (the source of wealth 財源) who actually conceives and raises that treasure in her womb is Vasudhara.

When we saw earlier that "for the male deity (Jambhala) to activate, he must meet the counterclockwise womb," the personal embodiment of that womb is the goddess Vasudhara.

Vasudhara's blessing, as a Yijing hexagram, can be called *Earth-Thunder, Return* (지뢰복 地雷復 ䷗).

Because it is the golden seed (single yang 一陽) conceived in Vasudhara's womb (Kun ☷).

Looking at the structure of Return (䷗), above (outside) is Kun (坤 ☷, earth, womb), and at the very bottom (first line) a single yang line (일양, Zhen ☳) has just been born.

In the dark earth of the winter solstice (동지 冬至) when the whole world is frozen solid (Kun-earth ☷ = Vasudhara's deep womb), the moment the first flame of life (single yang = Jambhala's seed syllable "Jam") finally begins to pulse with a "thump!" is Return.

It is the first life force of spring (일양시생) breaking up through the dark earth as Zhen-wood (震木 / Mao-wood 卯木).

In the embrace of the womb, Jambhala's seed (the syllable "Jam ཛཾ," or Vasudhara's seed syllable "Vas / Vam") takes the mother's nourishment and awakens as "single yang," then shoots up vigorously along the 3 o'clock direction (the position of eastern Mao-wood 卯木).

So to receive Vasudhara's blessing, take the hand seal of *Return* (지뢰복 ䷗).

Za Rahula's thunder: melting the bones of ghosts

The energy of Za Rahula (자 라훌라, གཟའ་རཱ་ཧུ་ལ་) is very sharp and ferocious, and it is warned that an unprepared practitioner who handles it suffers nervous-system disorders (wind illness, paralysis).

Inwardly, Rahula symbolizes sudden discharges of the autonomic nervous system, or the rough prana (wind qi 풍기 風氣) running wild while trapped in the left and right channels (ida and pingala). When this is integrated by an intense awakening of the central channel (sushumna / the penetrating vessel 충맥), it is transformed into the guardian power of transcendent awareness (Rigpa) that sees through every direction, like the image of Rahula with a thousand eyes.

It is the same principle as Eastern internal alchemy burning the yin demons (음마 陰魔), illusions of yin qi, or the three corpses and nine worms (삼시구충 三尸九蟲) and goblins (이매망량 魑魅魍魎) in the body with true fire (진화 眞火) and thunder rites (뇌법 雷法), turning them into nourishment for the yang spirit (양신 陽神).

The concept by which the Thunder-Sound Celestial Worthy (구천응원뇌성보화천존 九天應元雷聲普化天尊), supreme lord of the thunder rites of the Daoist Shenxiao (신소파 神霄派) and Qingwei (청미파 淸微派) schools, "melts the bones and shatters the forms" (銷骨碎形 / refining and delivering 煉度) of goblins and evil ghosts can be seen as exactly the same energy engineering as Za Rahula's thunderbolt-like subjugation (조복 調伏).

In the qi-science of Daoism and tantra, goblins and demonic obstacles (마장 魔障) are not mere illusions. They are masses of energy in which resentment, attachment, and skewed natural yin qi have clumped together strongly and acquired their own fixed information structure (skeleton).

The central axis of this hardened wave is the "ghost's bone" (귀골 鬼骨). As long as the bone remains, goblins scatter and then restore their form again, making mischief or causing illness.

Ordinary physical force or low-level spells cannot break this hard crystal of yin qi. The legend of Za Rahula, tamed by Padmasambhava

Rahula (Za Rahula) is not an object of popular devotion that ordinary Buddhists worship to pray for blessings. His nature carries an extremely dangerous and fierce energy that strikes the nervous system and causes eclipses.

Instead, he has been strictly honored as a "supreme protector" (Dharmapala) who guards the purity of the teaching and smashes practitioners' demonic obstacles in Nyingma, the oldest school of Tibetan Buddhism, and in its highest practice system, Dzogchen (the Great Perfection).

A very tragic and intense Tibetan local legend lies behind how the Indian Rahu, coming into Tibetan tantra, was transformed into the terrible, fierce wrathful deity "Za Rahula" seen in the image earlier.

In ancient Tibet (or northern India) there was a great yogi who devoted himself only to practice deep in the mountains. He was deeply respected by the queen (or a patron) of a kingdom and received offerings from her. But jealous courtiers falsely accused him to the king: "That practitioner is having an affair with the queen."

The enraged king, without investigating, seized the yogi, tortured him terribly, and burned him alive (or threw him into a pit of vipers). At the moment of death, the yogi, who had practiced purely his whole life, was seized by extreme rage at human folly and the injustice done to him.

"I will become the being who brings the most terrible calamities upon this foolish world!"

His fierce resentment combined with his amplified practice energy, and right after death he was reborn as "Za Rahula," a terrible demon king with nine heads, thousands of eyes, and a serpent's lower body. Carrying a bow and arrows, he flew through the sky shooting arrows that caused strokes, epilepsy, and terrible epidemics, and he became an object of terror who even blotted out the sun and moon.

When cosmic calamity broke out, the great teacher Padmasambhava (Guru Rinpoche), founder of Tibetan tantra, or Vajrapani, the incarnation of wrath, stepped in.

Padmasambhava did not destroy Rahula.

Instead, after subduing (조복) his vast energy of rage and karma with the power of the Dharma, he showed him the ultimate truth of the universe and awakened his original clear Buddha-nature.

Realizing that his rage came from dualistic illusion, Rahula knelt before Padmasambhava and vowed: "From now on I will use this mighty power not to destroy the Dharma but to crush the obstacles and enemies who obstruct the deepest teaching of tantra (Dzogchen)."

After that, Za Rahula became one of the three most powerful protectors of the Dzogchen tradition. The arrows he shoots are no longer calamities that sicken the innocent, but a weapon of compassion that pierces and kills exactly the "tangles of energy" and the life of the "ego" that obstruct a practitioner's awakening.

These stories show metaphorically that the energy Rahula governs is "suppressed fierce karma" and an "explosion of bioelectricity" that strikes the nervous system. Out of control, that powerful destructive force becomes stroke or paralysis (Rahula's arrows), but tuned by wisdom (Padmasambhava) it becomes the most powerful driving force to open the dimensional door of awakening. The essence of tantra is contained whole in this story.

Ida nadi (the left channel, the moon's path): flows along the left side of the spine; a yin (陰) energy governing the parasympathetic nervous system, coolness, intuition, memory (past karma), and inhalation.

When you pull hard with the head, "I want to be rich" or "I want to be healthy," the premise and fear "I'm lacking now (poor / sick)" inevitably cling to the bottom of the brain's dualistic structure like the back of a coin.

Just as pushing on a wall makes the wall push back with the same force, the more strongly you want light with a split consciousness (the brain), the more an exactly equal amount of darkness (the counter-effect) is cast behind your back (in the unconscious and unexpected reality) where your sight doesn't reach.

This is called the principle of "neither increasing nor decreasing" (부증불감 不增不減). Seen as a whole, it's a zero-sum game, neither growing nor shrinking.

By contrast, the "lower heart chakra" (the tiny space within the heart) at the center of the sternum is the one zero point where duality doesn't operate: a structure of unity (Oneness).

A furnace where upper and lower energies melt into one: when you draw in the two energies of heaven (yang, the upper triangle) and earth (yin, the lower triangle) through the breath and unite them in the heart chakra, a primordial state of unity opens in which the very opposition of yin and yang disappears (the Eastern "Supreme Pole" 황극 皇極, the Western singularity at the center of the torus).

In the space of the heart you know intuitively that all things are already connected as one and everything is already complete. So creation happens not through the ego's craving, "I lack, so I must have," but by naturally projecting images of already-complete joy, gratitude, and unconditional love from inside (the heart) to outside (the hologram of reality).

In the end, only the creative act of emptiness takes place, and you understand that the world is the dance of God.

So the secret of true attraction and creation can be summed up as: "Stop trying to manipulate reality with thought (the brain); send awareness down into the center of the chest (the lower heart chakra) and dream from the frequency of Oneness, which has no counter-effect."

The birth of Horus, from the union of yin and yang

1. Set's usurpation and the mutilation of Osiris

Osiris, god of fertility and king of Egypt, was killed through the jealousy and scheming of his brother Set. Set cut Osiris's body into 14 pieces and scattered them throughout Egypt.

2. Isis's search and magical restoration

Isis, Osiris's wife and the great goddess of magic, set out to find her husband's scattered body. She succeeded in finding and assembling all the pieces except one part, the genitals (eaten by a Nile fish called the oxyrhynchus). So Isis made magical genitals of gold (or clay), attached them to Osiris's body, and wrapped him as a mummy, restoring his body whole.

3. The breath of life and conception

Isis turned into a kite (or falcon) and circled over Osiris's body. With powerful wingbeats she raised a magic wind and breathed the breath of life into Osiris temporarily. Uniting with the revived Osiris, Isis at last succeeded in receiving his semen (seed), and thus conceived Horus.

4. Hiding and the birth of Horus

Osiris then left to become king of the underworld (the afterlife), and Isis fled from Set's eyes. She hid in Khemmis, the papyrus marshes of the Nile delta, and bore Horus alone. Isis protected her son by magic from threats such as the vipers and scorpions Set sent, and raised Horus in secret.

Talabya Kriya: stretching the frenulum instead of cutting it

The upper wall of the nasopharynx at the back of the throat is dense with vagus nerve endings and endocrine-regulating reflex points. Stimulating this area brings a state of deep relaxation and mental bliss.

For this, yoga traditionally does "Kechari Mudra" (the technique of turning the tongue back and up into the nasopharynx behind the throat).

In classical hatha yoga of the past, a surgical method of cutting the frenulum (the cord under the tongue) little by little with a knife was sometimes used,

but orthodox Kriya Yoga in the Lahiri Mahasaya tradition, instead of such dangerous methods, approaches it through Talabya Kriya, gradually lengthening the frenulum and strengthening the tongue muscles.

[Method]

1. Seal to the palate: stick not just the tip but the whole surface of the tongue broadly to the roof of the mouth (from the hard palate to the soft palate at the back). Draw out the air in the mouth to create a vacuum.

2. Open the jaw (stretching): keeping the tongue vacuum-stuck to the palate, slowly lower the jaw as far as possible. You'll feel a strong stimulus as the frenulum under the tongue is pulled taut.

3. Make the click (Release): when the jaw is fully open and the pressure reaches its limit, release the tongue from the palate so that a loud, clear suction pop (clicking sound), "ttak!" or "peok!", sounds in the mouth.

4. Repeat: counting this as one, repeat rhythmically 50 times.

— Ennio Nimis

In males, the Wolffian duct develops and the Müllerian duct regresses, remaining, as was pointed out earlier, as the empty "prostatic utricle (the male uterus)" in the middle of the prostate.

In females, the Müllerian duct develops into the uterus and vagina, and the Wolffian duct, which would have become the male organs, regresses. But this male seed doesn't disappear completely. Remarkably, it remains hidden for life as fine ducts along both sides of the cervix and the vaginal wall.

In medical terminology this is said to be called "Gartner's duct."

That is, traces of anima and animus remain biologically within our bodies.

The Vaishravana dharani from the Lotus Sutra

Vaishravana, the Buddha of the north, was originally a being who guarded the treasures in the earth. A being who guards treasures not yet revealed to the world and repels evil things.

"Ari Nari Nonari Anaro Nari Gunari"

The mantra of Vaishravana (the Heavenly King Who Hears Much, 다문천왕) from the "Dharani" chapter (陀羅尼品) of the *Lotus Sutra* (法華經).

The mantric power of this incantation carrying Vaishravana's protection looks simple on the surface, but within its wave is a fierce dance that cuts away evil energy.

Meaning of the mantra:

- *Ari Nari*: the image of dancing on high with a weapon, warning [evil beings] not to approach.

- *Nonari*: the majesty of dancing in the forest and proclaiming to bad beings.

- *Anaro*: unshakable wholeness.

- *Nari (nadi)*: the pulse of endless life force flowing in the heart.

- *Gunari*: a special guardian who surely protects us.

The greatest purpose of this mantra is to repel and protect so that you meet no worries whatsoever within a radius of a hundred yojanas (a distance so vast an arrow could fly it a hundred times).

It becomes the biggest, most dependable umbrella, keeping outside forces or evil maras (bad news, envy, fraud, etc.) that would take away wealth and abundance from even daring to approach the bounds of my life.

From the viewpoint of vocal qigong, this mantra, through the repeated strikes of its consonants, gives the nervous system a powerful "boundary alarm" and "vitality" at the same time.

"N" (*nari*, *nonari*): spinal vibration and the rising of the sympathetic nerves:

Pronouncing "n" vibrates the spine gently from the coccyx up and stimulates the sympathetic nerves. This relaxes the body while sharply raising the antennas of the senses. Rather than making the amygdala, the part of the brain that detects threats, tremble with anxiety, it helps norepinephrine release so you face the situation clearly and coolly, like a general taking the battlefield.

"R" (*aro*, *nari*, *gunari*): the turning of the microcosmic orbit and energy circulation. Pronouncing "r" strongly circulates (turns) the qi that rose up the spine. It speeds up stalled blood flow and cerebrospinal fluid, cleanly washes the brain's frontal lobe, stiffened by stress (cortisol), and sends the pulse of powerful life force round the whole body.

From the viewpoint of analytical psychology, reciting this mantra is an active meditation that summons the archetypes of the "Warrior" and the "Protector" from the depths of the unconscious.

The origin of the White-Robed Great Being dharani

The origin of the White-Robed Great Being dharani (백의대사신주 白衣大士神呪)

This mantra doesn't come from the orthodox Buddhist canon (정장 正藏), composed in India and translated into Chinese; it's a "people's dharani," born spontaneously and polished in the desperate lives of East Asian common people as it passed through China.

According to the best-known Chinese tale, long ago, when someone faced execution under a false accusation, or wandered at death's door with an incurable illness, the compassionate Avalokiteshvara (the White-Robed Great Being), dressed in white from head to toe, appeared in a dream.

The bodhisattva taught them a short incantation and said, "If you recite this incantation 10,000 times (or 12,000 times), you'll surely live." When they woke and recited it day and night in prison (or on their sickbed), they were miraculously pardoned or the illness was healed as if washed away.

[The bodhisattva] was indigenized as "the most familiar and compassionate mother, who doesn't stay in temples but comes down to the marketplace in white clothes and directly soothes the suffering of ordinary people."

Over thousands of years, countless people at the crossroads of life and death, or in desperate crises, have recited this mantra with the same sound ("Tadyatha Om Garabada…") and an earnest heart.

As that vast aspiration and its waves accumulated beyond time and space, the White-Robed Great Being dharani went beyond mere letters to form a powerful "energy field of healing and protection (morphogenetic field)."

The White-Robed Avalokiteshvara dharani, line by line

The White-Robed Avalokiteshvara dharani (白衣觀音神呪)

Namo Great Love, Great Compassion, Saving from Suffering and Hardship, Vast Spiritual Response, Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva Mahasattva
Namo Buddha, Namo Dharma, Namo Sangha, Namo Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, Saving from Suffering and Hardship

Tadyatha Om Garabada Garabada
Gahabada Ragabada Ragabada Svaha (×9)

Cheonrasin Jirasin Inrinan Nanrisin
Ilche Jaeang Hwawijin

Namo Maha Banya Baramil

1. Refuge and praise (relying on the Buddhas and bodhisattvas)

- Namo Great Love, Great Compassion, Saving from Suffering and Hardship, Vast Spiritual Response, Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva Mahasattva

An introduction expressing the resolve to lower oneself and rely wholly on the Three Jewels at Buddhism's core (the Buddha, the teaching, the monks) and on Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva.

- Namo Buddha, Namo Dharma, Namo Sangha, Namo Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, Saving from Suffering and Hardship

Buddha, Dharma, Sangha: taking refuge in the Three Jewels, Buddhism's three treasures (the Buddha, the Buddha's teaching, the community of monks).

2. The main dharani (proclaiming the mystic mantra)

This part transliterates Sanskrit into Chinese characters by sound; it's the core incantation, recited without translating the meaning, trusting the wave and mystic power of the sound itself.

Tadyatha Om Garabada Garabada Gahabada Ragabada Ragabada Svaha

3. Protection by the Dharma-guarding generals and extinguishing calamity (overcoming real-world hardship)

A powerful declaration that, through the power of Avalokiteshvara and the help of the generals (protective gods) of heaven and earth, all real-world calamities will be completely eliminated.

- Cheonrasin Jirasin Inrinan Nanrisin Ilche Jaeang Hwawijin

Cheonrasin (天羅神), Jirasin (地羅神): the gods of heaven and earth who protect as closely as heaven's net.
Inrinan (人離難), Nanrisin (難離神): gods who free people from the disasters arising among them and all kinds of tangled troubles.
Ilche jaeang hwawijin (一切災殃化爲塵): all calamities and hardships "turn to dust (化爲塵) and blow away." The most essential phrase for extinguishing bad luck.

4. Refuge in ultimate wisdom (conclusion toward awakening)

Going beyond the fortune-seeking level of simply avoiding real-world calamity, it ends with the resolve to attain perfect wisdom (awakening), the ultimate goal of Buddhism.

Namo Maha Banya Baramil
Maha: great, magnificent.
Banya (Prajna): wisdom that sees through the world as it is.
Baramil (Paramita): crossing to the other shore (the world of awakening), perfecting.
Interpretation: "Taking refuge in great and perfect wisdom, I will attain awakening."
